text: In the seventh year, in the fifth month, on the tenth day of the month, certain of the elders of Israel came to inquire of the LORD, and they sat down before me.
Then the word of the LORD came to me:
Son of man, speak to the elders of Israel and say to them: Thus says the Lord GOD: Have you come to inquire of me? As I live, I will not let you inquire of me, declares the Lord GOD.
Will you judge them? Will you judge them, son of man? Then confront them with the abominations of their fathers,

and say to them: Thus says the Lord GOD: On the day I chose Israel, I raised my hand in an oath to the offspring of the house of Jacob and made myself known to them in the land of Egypt. I raised my hand and swore to them, saying, I am the LORD your God.
On that day I swore to them that I would bring them out of the land of Egypt into a land I had searched out for them, a land flowing with milk and honey, the most beautiful of all lands.
And I said to them: Each of you, throw away the detestable things your eyes are set on, and do not defile yourselves with the idols of Egypt. I am the LORD your God.

But they rebelled against me and refused to listen to me. Not one of them threw away the detestable things their eyes were set on, and they did not abandon the idols of Egypt. So I said I would pour out my wrath upon them and spend my anger against them in the midst of the land of Egypt.

But I acted for the sake of my name, so that it would not be profaned in the sight of the nations among whom they lived, in whose sight I had made myself known to them by bringing them out of the land of Egypt.
So I brought them out of the land of Egypt and led them into the wilderness.
I gave them my statutes and made known to them my rules, by which anyone who does them shall live.
I also gave them my Sabbaths, as a sign between me and them, so they would know that I am the LORD who sanctifies them.

But the house of Israel rebelled against me in the wilderness. They did not walk in my statutes; they rejected my rules, by which anyone who does them shall live; and they utterly profaned my Sabbaths. So I said I would pour out my wrath upon them in the wilderness and make an end of them.
But I acted for the sake of my name, so that it would not be profaned in the sight of the nations, before whose eyes I had brought them out.
Moreover, I swore to them in the wilderness that I would not bring them into the land I had given them, a land flowing with milk and honey, the most beautiful of all lands—
because they rejected my rules and did not walk in my statutes and profaned my Sabbaths, for their hearts went after their idols.
Yet my eye spared them from destruction, and I did not make a full end of them in the wilderness.
And I said to their children in the wilderness: Do not walk in the statutes of your fathers, do not keep their rules, and do not defile yourselves with their idols.
I am the LORD your God. Walk in my statutes, keep my rules, and do them.
Keep my Sabbaths holy, and let them be a sign between me and you, so you may know that I am the LORD your God.

But the children rebelled against me. They did not walk in my statutes, nor were they careful to keep my rules, by which anyone who does them shall live; they profaned my Sabbaths. So I said I would pour out my wrath upon them and spend my anger against them in the wilderness.

versions.text: But the children rebelled against me. They did not walk in my statutes, and they did not keep my rules by doing them, by which anyone who does them shall live; they profaned my Sabbaths. So I said I would pour out my wrath upon them and spend my anger against them in the wilderness.
versions.explanation: The doubled "by doing them, by which anyone who does them" is clumsy when read aloud. Tightening it preserves the sense of לַעֲשׂוֹת אוֹתָם while keeping the rhythm of the parallel clauses in vv. 11 and 13.

text: But I held back my hand and acted for the sake of my name, so that it would not be profaned in the sight of the nations, before whose eyes I had brought them out.
Moreover, I swore to them in the wilderness that I would scatter them among the nations and disperse them through the lands,
because they had not kept my rules, had rejected my statutes, had profaned my Sabbaths, and had fixed their eyes on the idols of their fathers.
So I also gave them statutes that were not good and rules by which they could not live.
I declared them defiled through their gifts, in that they offered up every firstborn, so that I might horrify them, so they would know that I am the LORD.

versions.text: I let them defile themselves through their gifts, in that they offered up all their firstborn, so that I might horrify them, so they would know that I am the LORD.
versions.explanation: The Hebrew verb וָאֲטַמֵּא is first-person causative ("I defiled/declared unclean them"), parallel to "I gave them statutes that were not good" in v. 25. Rendering it as "I let them defile themselves" removes God as the agent and weakens the deliberate, difficult parallelism of the passage. Also, פֶּטֶר רָחַם is "every firstborn" (singular collective), not "all their firstborn." A footnote could note that "offered up" refers to passing children through the fire.

text: Therefore, son of man, speak to the house of Israel and say to them: Thus says the Lord GOD: In this also your fathers blasphemed me, by dealing treacherously with me.

For when I brought them into the land that I swore to give them, they saw every high hill and every leafy tree, and there they offered their sacrifices and presented offerings that provoked me; there they sent up their pleasing aromas and poured out their drink offerings.
So I said to them: What is this high place to which you keep going? And its name is called Bamah to this day. [Footnote: "Bamah" is the Hebrew word for "high place."]

versions.text: So I said to them: What is this high place to which you go? And it is called Bamah to this day.
versions.explanation: The wordplay between "high place" (בָּמָה) earlier in the verse and the name "Bamah" is invisible to a hearer; a brief footnote clarifies it. "To which you keep going" also better reflects the participle הַבָּאִים (ongoing action).

text: Therefore say to the house of Israel: Thus says the Lord GOD: Will you defile yourselves after the manner of your fathers and prostitute yourselves after their detestable things?

When you present your gifts, when you make your children pass through the fire, you defile yourselves with all your idols to this day. And shall I let you inquire of me, O house of Israel? As I live, declares the Lord GOD, I will not let you inquire of me.
What rises up in your spirit will never come to pass—you who say, "We will be like the nations, like the clans of the lands, serving wood and stone."

versions.text: What is in your mind shall never come to pass—when you say, "We will be like the nations, like the tribes of other lands, serving wood and stone."
versions.explanation: עֹלָה עַל־רוּחֲכֶם is literally "what comes up in your spirit," which is stronger and reads better aloud than "what is in your mind"; "other" in "other lands" is an addition not in the Hebrew, and מִשְׁפְּחוֹת is better rendered "clans." Also, "when you say" is better as a relative clause referring to the people themselves (אֲשֶׁר אַתֶּם אֹמְרִים).

text: As I live, declares the Lord GOD, surely with a mighty hand and an outstretched arm and with wrath poured out I will reign over you.
I will bring you out from the peoples and gather you from the lands where you were scattered, with a mighty hand and an outstretched arm and with wrath poured out.
I will bring you into the wilderness of the peoples, and there I will enter into judgment with you face to face.
As I entered into judgment with your fathers in the wilderness of the land of Egypt, so I will enter into judgment with you, declares the Lord GOD.
I will make you pass under the shepherd's rod, and I will bring you into the bond of the covenant.

versions.text: I will make you pass under the rod, and I will bring you into the bond of the covenant.
versions.explanation: The image is of a shepherd counting his flock under his staff (cf. Lev 27:32); making the shepherd imagery explicit aids oral comprehension, since "pass under the rod" alone can be misheard as mere punishment. A footnote on מָסֹרֶת ("bond," a rare word, possibly "discipline" or "binding obligation") could also be helpful.

text: I will purge out from among you the rebels and those who transgress against me. I will bring them out of the land where they sojourn, but they shall not enter the land of Israel. Then you will know that I am the LORD.

As for you, house of Israel, thus says the Lord GOD: Go and serve your idols, every one of you, if you will not listen to me; but afterward you shall no longer profane my holy name with your gifts and your idols.

versions.text: As for you, house of Israel, thus says the Lord GOD: Go and serve your idols, every one of you, if you will not listen to me. But you shall no longer profane my holy name with your gifts and your idols.
versions.explanation: The Hebrew adverb וְאַחַר ("and afterward") is left untranslated. It marks the turn from the ironic command to the promise that they will cease profaning God's name, and its loss weakens the sense of the verse.

text: For on my holy mountain, on the high mountain of Israel, declares the Lord GOD, there all the house of Israel, all of them, shall serve me in the land. There I will accept them, and there I will require your contributions and the firstfruits of your offerings, with all your holy things.

versions.text: For on my holy mountain, on the high mountain of Israel, declares the Lord GOD, there all the house of Israel, all of them, shall serve me in the land. There I will accept them, and there I will require your contributions and the choicest of your gifts, with all your holy offerings.
versions.explanation: רֵאשִׁית means "first, firstfruits," a cultic term for the first portion given to God; "choicest" loses that sense. קָדְשֵׁיכֶם is broader than "holy offerings" and is better as "your holy things."

text: As a pleasing aroma I will accept you, when I bring you out from the peoples and gather you from the lands where you were scattered. And through you I will show myself holy in the sight of the nations.
Then you will know that I am the LORD, when I bring you into the land of Israel, the land that I swore to give to your fathers.
There you will remember your ways and all the deeds by which you defiled yourselves, and you will loathe yourselves for all the evils you have committed.
And you will know that I am the LORD, when I deal with you for my name's sake and not according to your evil ways or your corrupt deeds, O house of Israel, declares the Lord GOD.
